items.title: Doors of Cairo — Forever Is Now 05
items.description: Doors of Cairo is Vhils' large-scale installation for Forever Is Now 05 (Art D'Égypte's annual open-air exhibition), staged beside the Pyramids of Giza in November 2025. The piece is built from reclaimed wooden doors collected across Portugal and Cairo, then reassembled into a 14.5 × 5.5 × 5 m freestanding monument supported by metal scaffolding. Each door carries the marks of countless hands — fragments of homes, shops and quiet corners of the city — turning everyday architectural objects into a temporary threshold, a portal between past and present, between individual memory and collective history. Placed in the desert beside the pyramids, the doors shed their literal function and become a meditation on shelter, intimacy, and the architectures of human presence. Curated and produced by Nadine Abdelghaffar Documentary photography by José Pando Lucas.

items.title: Fábrica 390
items.description: Fábrica 390 features a large-scale carved portrait of an elderly woman, her weathered face emerging from layers of plaster and exposed brick. Geometric folk-textile motifs frame the figure, chiselled directly into the wall surface alongside the subtractive portraiture. The work fuses architectural archaeology with vernacular craft traditions, anchoring individual memory to material and cultural heritage.

items.title: Strates Urbains
items.description: Strates Urbaines (Urban Layers) is Vhils' largest permanent commission to date — a monumental azulejo mural at the Aéroport d'Orly station of the Grand Paris Express, inaugurated 19 June 2024. Spanning 35 metres in length and 7 metres in height across levels –1 and –2 of the new station, the work is composed of approximately 11,132 traditional Portuguese ceramic tiles, hand-carved over 14 months. Faces of Parisians emerge from and dissolve back into the fabric of the city — the Eiffel Tower, blueprint maps of Paris, iconic buildings — exploring the reciprocal shaping process between a city and its inhabitants. The cobalt-blue glazed surfaces are deliberately mirror-like, so each traveller passing through the station sees their own reflection layered onto the portraits and the urban scenes for the 15-30 seconds they spend in front of the wall. The station was designed by architects Bernard Baret and François Tamisier (Chief Architect of Aéroports de Paris). Vhils will present a second part of the work in 2027 for the inauguration of Line 18 between Massy-Palaiseau and Orly. Sponsored by Ardian.

items.title: The Meaning of Life (International Space Station)
items.description: In September 2015, Vhils' site-specific portrait of Danish ESA astronaut Andreas Mogensen travelled to the International Space Station — the first artwork ever installed in space. Printed on micro-perforated PVC film and conceived to fit precisely into the Cupola module — the European observatory window from which astronauts can see the entirety of Earth — the work let the light, colour and movement of the planet pass directly through Mogensen's portrait as the station orbited at 28,800 km/h. The piece was conceived as part of "The Meaning of Life," a documentary by Portuguese filmmaker Miguel Gonçalves Mendes that follows seven people, one of them Mogensen, the first Danish astronaut. The collaboration was a joint initiative between Vhils, the documentary team and the European Space Agency, marking the first time a contemporary visual artist created a permanent, site-specific intervention aboard the ISS.

Vhils and his crew (locally known as The Dalton Brothers) chiselled portraits of historical figures from Vardø: a fisherman portrait carved into the painted render of a wooden building (a first for Vhils, who normally works on concrete) and a baker portrait on a more standard concrete wall.

items.description: Sentinela is a large-scale public mural carved by Vhils on a building facade along the route to the beaches of Costa da Caparica, in the municipality of Almada, Portugal, completed in early April 2026. The work pays tribute to António Gonçalves Ribeiro, the lifeguard known as "Tarzan da Caparica," who is credited with saving more than 300 people over roughly five decades of service on the local beaches. The carved portrait is based on a 1964 photograph of Ribeiro and was produced using the artist's characteristic bas-relief technique of removing layers of the wall's surface to reveal the image. The intervention was commissioned by GDMA - Reabilitação e Construção, the owner of the building.

items.title: Tangible (SEAT × Vhils)
items.description: "Tangible" is a large-scale public sculpture by Alexandre Farto (Vhils), unveiled in October 2018 on the waterfront at Cascais Marina, Portugal, as a collaboration with the carmaker SEAT marking the 15th anniversary of SEAT Portugal. Weighing roughly 15 tonnes and built over the course of about a year from cement, fibreglass and silicone over a steel armature, the work reinterprets the lines of the SEAT Arona, fusing the front of the vehicle with horizontal building forms at the rear that resolve into the shape of an eye. The piece extends the artist's enquiry into the relationship between cities and their inhabitants, conceived as a kind of contemporary fossil intended to outlast its own era and be rediscovered in the future. The project was developed in the orbit of the Underdogs platform and the future Museum of Urban and Contemporary Art in Cascais (MARCC).

items.description: For a special collector double issue titled "Le monde selon Vhils," published on 7 May 2026, the French weekly Courrier International (Le Monde Group) invited Alexandre Farto, known as Vhils, to take over the magazine — the first time in its history that an artist was given its pages. Vhils produced four distinct covers, each a layered-poster portrait whose face was revealed by cutting and tearing into the printed paper, applying his signature "soft, poetic destruction" to the newspaper itself rather than to a wall. items.title: Scratching the Surface
items.description: In January 2010, the Portuguese artist Vhils (Alexandre Farto) carried out a public intervention in Moscow as part of his ongoing Scratching the Surface project, carving large-scale human portraits directly into the worn plaster and surface layers of existing walls. Working in his characteristic bas-relief technique with chisel, drill and other removal tools rather than paint, he excavated the building's accumulated layers to reveal the image hidden within the wall. The Moscow work belongs to the wider Scratching the Surface series, which by this period had spread across cities including London, New York and locations in Italy and Portugal, treating the urban fabric itself as both material and subject.

items.description: Scratching the Surface (Brussels) is a permanent public mural created by Portuguese artist Alexandre Farto, known as Vhils, on a wall of the Léopold playground at Rue Léopold 27 in central Brussels. Using his signature subtractive technique, the artist and his team carved a monumental bas-relief portrait into the wall over the course of roughly a week, removing surface layers with tools ranging from jackhammers and chisels to acid. The composition incorporates a delicately etched carnation flower, a reference to Portugal's 1974 Carnation Revolution and its peaceful defence of freedom and democracy. Inaugurated on 26 June 2024, the work was conceived to coincide with Vhils's solo exhibition Multitude at the MIMA Museum, bridging the institution and the surrounding urban space.

items.title: Passage 46, Theater Freiburg

items.description: In September 2014, Vhils (Alexandre Farto) created a permanent interior wall work for Passage 46, the music/art/bar space inside Theater Freiburg (the renovated former Jackson-Pollock-Bar), in Freiburg im Breisgau, Germany. Applying his subtractive technique to the bar's interior walls — chiselling and chipping away the plaster surface — he revealed a series of bas-relief faces in his signature white-on-substrate idiom, resulting in a carved triptych of illuminated panels behind the bar. The piece was unveiled with a vernissage as part of the opening of the new Passage 46 in autumn 2014. (Henrik Springmann coordinated the Passage 46 project; the artist was documented working there by Badische Zeitung, 10 Sep 2014.)

items.address: Serra de Leomil, Moimenta da Beira (Viseu district), Portugal
items.description: WindArt is a 2016 public-art project on the Serra de Leomil ridge in Moimenta da Beira (Viseu district), Portugal, in which Vhils (Alexandre Farto) and Joana Vasconcelos each transformed a ~100-metre-tall wind turbine in the Parque Eólico do Douro Sul into a monumental artwork — among the tallest contemporary artworks in the world by height. Commissioned by Ancora Wind Energia Eólica SA as a tribute to renewable energy, Vhils wrapped his turbine in a graphic extrapolation of the natural textures of the region's tree species — bark and his signature torn-poster/relief vocabulary in black on white — together with a surveying human eye, connecting the work to the elements that give life and energy to the site. (Vasconcelos's neighbouring turbine, 'Gone with the Wind', is a separate, colourful work by a different artist.)
